quest.title: Fated Warrior
quest.description: The scryglass reflects visions of the future, the wolf spirit harbors memories of the past...\nThe threads of fate are ever-changing.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

chapter.title: To Those Who Embark on the Expedition

talks.objective: Attend the meeting at Favonius Keep

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After updating Varka on the situation in Mondstadt, you explain the relationship between the God of the North Wind and the Bloodstained Knight to the attendees...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...And that's where things stand. The Wild Hunt is no longer under the Rächer of Solnari's control, but it has been reborn from the ashes and is now launching widespread attacks.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Intel from the Frostmoon Scions and the Curatorium of Secrets corroborates this. No disturbances have been detected in the space where Rerir resides. What we are facing here is a completely new foe.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Summarizing current situation... To confirm — the present leader of the Wild Hunt is the creature resembling a wolf? Andrius, God of the North Wind...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: More precisely, it's the external will that has seized control of Andrius's spirit... namely Roland, the Bloodstained Knight.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa, hold on, I'm completely lost! Isn't Roland some Mondstadter from, like, 500 years ago?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: How'd he suddenly get wrapped up with a god from a thousand years in the past AND the present-day Wild Hunt?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Allow us to explain that part.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Are you familiar with compensation mechanisms? When an organism sustains damage, relevant tissues will undergo changes to offset the loss of function...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: For example, when one kidney is damaged, the other will be strengthened to compensate. Or, when a main artery is blocked, the collateral vessels become more active...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Similarly, when the Wild Hunt lost their leader, the Abyss harnessed the memories that flow throughout the Ley Lines to fashion a new one, fit for the present circumstances.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: That new leader is a mirror image of Roland, the Bloodstained Knight.

choices.text: So that wasn't the real Roland...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Right. No matter how strong the compensation is, it will never quite match the functionality of the original organ.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: The Roland replica can't possibly imitate Rerir's overwhelming power, nor his ability to disguise himself as others.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: So, the Abyss made use of the connection between Roland and Boreas to compensate for this lack of power.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: The replica corrupted and took control of Andrius as he slumbered by the bank of Amsvartnir, ultimately manifesting as the giant beast that you all witnessed.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: ...However, exactly why the Abyss chose Roland to mimic — and indeed, how it was able to do so — remains unclear.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hmm. I guess he must've gotten caught up with the Abyss or Nod-Krai somehow during his wanderings through Teyvat... But we can keep those questions on the back burner.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, Paimon gets all that... but what did you mean when you said we can't kill him right now?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: We can't kill him right now, because a dead god may prove more dangerous than a living one.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: From intelligence gathered during the expedition, we have reason to believe that the power released when a god is felled can have catastrophic consequences for us mortals.

choices.text: (Like when the tower fell in Stormterror's Lair...)

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Worse still, the wrath that remains after a god's passing becomes a source of endless turmoil... Once god remains contaminate the land, they will persist for thousands of years.

choices.text: (Like the Tatarigami on Yashiori Island and Tatarasuna...)

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: This land has already been ravaged by the Wild Hunt. If we add god remains to the mix, it'll be like adding salt to an open wound, placing everyone who lives here in perilous danger.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Query... While I can indeed find records of disasters caused by god remains in my database, there also appear to be cases of gods dying naturally with no ill effects.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: In Natlan, the passing of the Pyro Archon's flame is a common occurrence throughout history, and even the part of Andrius who remains in Mondstadt has experienced death once before, has he not?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Great question — glad you asked. Honorary Knight, you said Lupus Boreas gave you a token to pass onto me? Please present it now — it should help explain things faster.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...Come forth, Boreas.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: ...This form has come to the end of its time. I'm afraid I can accompany you no further on your journey.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: My soul will fall into silence, and my power will flow into the Ley Lines of this land... Perhaps this is all that a wolf can hope to do for humankind.

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: Do not grieve for me, for this is the end I have chosen. Instead, remember that one day, your wandering, too, must come to an end... Where, and when shall that be?

response.speaker: Boreas
response.text: ...A final wish before I slumber? ...Hm, sing me a song. That melody you so often hummed in the taverns.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What was that?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: You saw it too? You must have keen powers of perception... Not that it surprises me.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: That was Boreas's final thoughts before merging with the Ley Lines. It's the reason Mondstadt remains unharmed by his god remains.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: In his final moments, he made a choice to give everything he was to the Ley Lines, all to protect Mondstadt from harm...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...Sounds like Andrius spent thousands of years searching for his place in the world, too...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Yes, and now our task is to return the answer he found, the decision he made, to Andrius's heart.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Only then can he break free from the corruption and control of the Abyss, and make that decision once more...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...To merge himself with the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I see... I would say that planting thoughts inside the mind of a god sounds a little far-fetched, but since it was his own wish to begin with... it sounds feasible to me.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Wait, we already have a perfect solution? Then why are we even having this meeting? Let's go do this thing!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha... If only it were that simple. Unfortunately, this one thought alone is unlikely to be powerful enough to break through the Abyss's control and reach Andrius's heart.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...We need to find a way to make the thought within this sword stronger and more resilient.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: For now, Boreas needs all his remaining strength to fight against the Abyssal corruption to Mondstadt's Ley Lines. He can't afford to send us any more of his power.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: However, since his form was unstable during his journey with the first Knight of Boreas, many Wolf Spirit fragments were left behind along the way...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: If we can collect those fragments, we can use them to strengthen the decision to merge with the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... So we need to retrace his steps and look for random fragments? But they could be anywhere between Nod-Krai and Mondstadt! It'll be like looking for a needle in a haystack!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, you don't need to worry about that. There's a few fragments left to gather in Nod-Krai, but apart from that...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Most of them are already inside this sword. I've been collecting them during the whole expedition.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait, really?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I mean, it's an expedition, not a stroll in the park... Each step of the way, we've been hard at work planning for every possible contingency.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Not just the Wild Hunt and the Abyss... But ancient gods remaining in Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Sounds like this plan was a long time in the making... It's almost as if you... foresaw the future?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: As a matter of fact, I did — I caught a glimpse of fate's reflection. But I can't take credit for it. It was all thanks to the help of a few fri{RUBY#[D]scryglass}ends...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Still, all I foresaw was that an Abyssal calamity was brewing in the North... Had I known more, we could have saved a lot of energy.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Instead, we've had to make best guesses, prepare for every possible scenario. If all that preparation went to waste, all the better for it — but anything that proved useful, we knew we'd be grateful for down the line.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And sure enough, now it's proving useful.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Sure is. Just one crucial step remains: We need to gather the last few Wolf Spirit fragments scattered around Nod-Krai, and use them to make the thought within this sword as strong as it can possibly be.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: According to what Boreas told me before we left Mondstadt, his form was at its most unstable at the beginning of his journey. That means, the fragments here should be the most powerful ones.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: But of course, we've been tied up fighting battles since the day we set foot in Nod-Krai — first with the Wild Hunt, then with The Doctor... So, it wasn't until recently that we were finally able to confirm the status of the Wolf Spirit fragments. We now know there are three left to find.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, so three more mini-expeditions to go...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I managed to gather one fragment before Roland reappeared. I also have a confirmed location for the second, which I'll take care of in short order.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: As for the third fragment, we've identified a general search area to focus on, but we'll need all hands on deck to pinpoint the exact location.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wow. You've made a lot of progress already!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: The final snag is that since our foe is a replica of Roland, he too will be aware of Andrius's history. He's sure to try and sabotage our plans by any means at his disposal... So everyone needs to bring their A-game!

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: With our foe being from Mondstadt... It's our duty as Mondstadters to defeat him.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: And since the Wild Hunt is involved, the Lightkeepers will provide their full support.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: The Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop will also help in any way we can.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (Uhh... So what do they need me here for? Wait, I think maybe I signed a contract at some point... Didn't exactly scrutinize it, though. I—I mean, who actually reads those things anyway, right?)

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Ahh, great... Knew I could count on you all. Lastly, our friend from the Curatorium of Secrets will provide intel and relay battlefield communications. Looking at you, Jahoda!

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: So you'll be darting back and forth across the battlefield, dodging the Wild Hunt and the shadow of an ancient god? I'm impressed by your courage, Miss Jahoda.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Rating for Jahoda updated. Higher-quality ingredients will be used to prepare your future meals.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (...Darn it! I shoulda known this payday wouldn't come that easy!)

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I'll deal with the second Wolf Spirit fragment, which we already know the location of. The moment you make any progress with fragment three, be sure to give me an update.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, could you join me in retrieving fragment two? I have a feeling that your unique constitution might come in handy.

choices.text: Sure. I was just about to ask what my job was.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Alright. Time is of the essence, let's move out, people! Dismissed!

choices.text: I'll follow your lead, Grand Master.
(Or the karmic debt borne by the Yakshas for millennia...)
(Or when the humans turned to salt beneath Sal Terrae...)
But rather an Abyssal imitation?

talks.objective: Go to the Wolf Spirit's location

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: #Hey, good to see you again, {NICKNAME}. Oh, Boss Nef asked me to pass on a message!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: She went to see Lauma and Columbina at the Frostmoon Scions. Apparently, there haven't been any changes to that space the Rächer of Solnari's in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That means, the recent Wild Hunt attacks have nothing to do with Rerir, right? Whew, that's a relief... Paimon doesn't fancy facing him again!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: They're keeping a close watch on it just in case. With so many moon experts on the case, we're in pretty safe hands, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, Lauma and Columbina asked me to pass on a message, too: "Focus on the enemy you are facing. The moon will protect you all!"

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...You know something? These Knights of Favonius are paying me a pretty nice sum to deliver a few simple messages... Hehe, Varka's a generous guy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this what we're looking for? Um, what do we do with it?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I once got Boreas to explain to me how he stores his soul inside objects. All I need to do is transfer it to my sw{RUBY#[S]claws of steel}ord.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Just like back at the camp... but this time, you'd best step back a bit. Just in case.

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Knight
dialogues.text: ...So you're saying you don't know how to love people, and you don't understand human love either? Pff...

dialogues.speaker: Boreas
dialogues.text: ...Why do you laugh?

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Knight
dialogues.text: Sorry, I just think... the fact you're ruminating on this is all the proof you need that you have love in your heart.

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Knight
dialogues.text: I have a funny feeling that by the time this journey ends... you'll have found your own answer to the question of how to love...

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: No, you're wrong. There is no redemption at the end of this path.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: ...Even if I am stained black with blood, my conscience will remain as white as snow.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: If pledging allegiance to the Abyss is the only way to sever the injustice of fate, then I shall serve in its name.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Argh...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Varka...!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Sure enough, this place has been corrupted by "Roland's" will... Whew... I'm fine — I was prepared for this. It wasn't enough to pose a serious threat.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: We got here just in time. The fragment hasn't been fully corrupted yet. Assuming we can undo the damage, it should still be usable.

choices.text: So that's why you brought me along...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hmm... Purifying the Abyssal corruption would definitely be a safe approach. But that's not the only reason I wanted you to come.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Could you try... reversing the corruption? Not "purifying" it, exactly, but separating out the "Roland" part from the Wolf Spirit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... keep the Roland part intact as well as the Wolf Spirit part? Why would you wanna do that?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Firstly, to test whether it's possible... And secondly, to view Roland's memories. As they say, "know thyself, know thy enemy" — understanding our foe is our surest path to defeating him.

choices.text: This is a little unexpected...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Lemme think, how was it explained to me... Ah, yes: "Focus on a single thought within the thousand winds, capture that unique wisp before it blows away."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I have no idea what that means!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hahaha! Actually, neither do I!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh, sounds like something a certain Tone-Deaf Bard would come up with when he can't think of anything meaningful to say... Wait, don't tell Paimon that's what actually happened!?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I thought it might mean something to you... Never mind, I'll explain it in more human terms.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, when you were in Natlan, you went "fishing" for ancient names, correct?

choices.text: Yes actually, sort of...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: If I'm not mistaken, the Night Kingdom was like a river flowing with concepts, and you were trying to capture the concept belonging to a particular ancient name... I'm thinking, the same basic principles should apply here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, but back then, we had a "boat" and a "net"... This time, we don't have anything at all!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Eh, this Wolf Spirit fragment is like a puddle compared to the Night Kingdom — no need for a boat. As for a net... This is what I've heard:

response.speaker: Varka's Memories
response.text: "Thoughts and emotions are like interwoven threads — they can create a net, or they can create a rope. They can separate love from hatred, and they can bind objects and events together."

response.speaker: Varka's Memories
response.text: "...Thought is the anchor for a being's existence, through which emotions are drawn forth."

choices.text: Okay, I think I'm kind of starting to get the idea...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, we barely know anything about Roland. How are we supposed to use thoughts to anchor him?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Well... Maybe you could try this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is it? It looks old and tattered...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: It's an unsent letter written by the "Wolf Pup" Rostam, Knight of Boreas, from 500 years ago. It was meant for his disciple, the "White Knight" Roland.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's a heck of a thing to have sitting in your back pocket...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: After Rostam lost his life in the Abyssal calamity, Roland left Mondstadt to wander Teyvat. Grand Master Arundolyn had wanted to deliver this letter to him...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: But trying to track Roland down was like chasing a sha{RUBY#[D]Rostam}dow. H{RUBY#[S]Arundolyn}e never did find him. And so, this letter has been sitting at the Knights of Favonius headquarters ever since.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Quite the antique, then... But how exactly is it supposed to anchor Roland?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha... I'm honestly not sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! What happened to Mr. plans for every contingency? You're just making this up as you go along!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Heh... What can I say — some people like to wait till they've got all their ducks in a row before taking the first step, but I prefer to dive on in and plan as I go. I've been doing it that way for the whole expedition.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: But anyway, don't they say that poetry and letters were humanity's earliest means of expressing their thoughts? Can't hurt to give it a try, surely?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We might as well see what happens...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Whoa... It actually worked?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You really are making this up as you go along!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: So the assimilation of souls really can be reversed... Just like he said...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Got him!

response.speaker: Roland
response.text: ...If what you say is true...

response.speaker: Roland
response.text: The monsters I've slain, the justice I've sought to uphold... For mortals to escape this tragic fate, there is only one path.

response.speaker: Roland
response.text: A great and ancient kingdom was wrongfully cursed, turning its inhabitants into monsters.

response.speaker: Roland
response.text: The code of chivalry tolerates not such injustice.

response.speaker: Roland
response.text: If Abyss be thy name, I pledge to you my loyalty.
...And that is where the Bloodstained Knight's tale came to an end. With that, he bade his humanity farewell.
...I daresay you must find it quite ironic, Knight of Boreas?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...That eye... Dainsleif? No... It bore a striking resemblance, but that wasn't him.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: While we gazed into the past, he was gazing right back at us... Could it be...?

choices.text: The Visionary...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: So that's what happened. After leaving Mondstadt and wandering the land, Roland ventured underground and saw a revelation from The Visionary.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Once he had learned of Khaenri'ah's fate, he saw the gods' judgment as the greatest injustice... So he surrendered himself to the Abyss...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...Giving them his knowledge, his power, his everything... That's why the Abyss can replicate him!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh... Does this mean we have to take on The Visionary this time?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (No... The founder of the Abyss Order was once shown a revelation... Based on his experience, at least...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...The Visionary is unlikely to intervene directly.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I'm inclined to agree. If our enemy could see the future, both the Wild Hunt and Roland would be acting with far more lethal precision.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: But even without The Visionary's input, Roland still has an intel advantage we can't afford to underestimate...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Every minion of the Wild Hunt serves as Roland's eyes and ears. We need to think one step ahead if we want to out-maneuver him.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: And on that note — I have a plan I want to discuss with you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Now? Why didn't you bring it up during the meeting?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, well, the fewer people who know, the less likely it is to get leaked. Besides, it wasn't a fully formed plan back then...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Varka explains his plan...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...Ah, that about covers it. Sorry to ask so much of you again.

choices.text: No way!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: No plan is free of risks. At least this one actually gives us a shot at fully eliminating the danger posed by this ancient god. Surely that's gotta make the risk worth taking?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But there's no guarantee it'll work...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...If I fail, Anselm and Albedo can take the reins. Not to mention we still have Jean in Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There has to be another way! Like a... backup backup-plan...?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: If only there were — but I don't think our enemy will give us enough time to find one.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Hey! Are you guys done here yet?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Ah, Jahoda! Yes, we've successfully retrieved the Wolf Spirit fragment here. Any progress with fragment three?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Nope — it's a total disaster! More Wild Hunt monsters than I've seen in my whole life! We need backup urgently, come quick!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Come on — we're out of time. You'll just have to trust me on this one!

choices.text: ...You're making too many decisions on your own.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, what can I say? I'm not the Grand Master for nothing! I'm counting on you, Honorary Knight.

choices.text: ...You're putting me in a difficult position here.
It's too dangerous!
Vedrfolnir!
...But maybe I'm not. It's hard to say.
But I wasn't the one doing the fishing.
I've never even tried this before...
You want me to purify it?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Speaking of contingency plans... I now recall that Varka also made a contingency plan when he asked me to deliver that letter.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Hmm, perhaps I should ask Aino to prepare some additional backup modules for me.

dialogues.speaker: Ekbert
dialogues.text: Grand Master! Honorary Knight! Thank goodness you're here!

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Be careful! There's no end to these monsters... however many we kill, more keep coming!

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: They've had us penned in so far, but now you're here, maybe we can try getting to the source, which is hidden in the mist. That way, we should be able to cut off the Wild Hunt's reinforcements!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Oh yeah? Then we'll leave that to you! Hey! Everyone hear that? We need to hold the line. Time to give 'em a taste of the Knights of Favonius fighting spirit!

dialogues.speaker: Knights
dialogues.text: ...Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Phew... I'm glad that's finally over.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Use this time to catch your breath, and fill me in on everything you've learned.

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: We've narrowed down the search area for the final fragment to this zone here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes! Now it feels like we're finally closing in on our target!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I'll say. We're sure to face fierce resistance from the Wild Hunt, though... Do you still have the strength to keep fighting with us?

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: Absolutely! Good to go, Grand Master!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Much obliged. Alright, the target is just up ahead! Move out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! It's the Wild Hunt! C'mon, let's go help!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Something's not right... The Wild Hunt's offensive doesn't seem to be getting any weaker as the battle goes on... Are they getting reinforcements from somewhere?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Don't get dragged into the enemy's rhythm! Logistics Company, scout out the area — look for terrain we can use to our advantage!

dialogues.speaker: Erminie
dialogues.text: Yes, sir! Reporting in, sir — we've identified viable sites for deploying explosives!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Good. Wait for my signal!

talks.objective: Support the Knights of Favonius' squad

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! It's the Wild Hunt! C'mon, let's go help!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Something's not right... The Wild Hunt's offensive doesn't seem to be getting any weaker as the battle goes on... Are they getting reinforcements from somewhere?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Don't get dragged into the enemy's rhythm! Logistics Company, scout out the area — look for terrain we can use to our advantage!

dialogues.speaker: Erminie
dialogues.text: Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Erminie
dialogues.text: Reporting in, sir — we've identified viable sites for deploying explosives!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Good. Wait for my signal!

talks.objective: Command the Logistics Company to set up traps

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Short-distance propulsion module on cooldown... 15 minutes until next departure.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: #Switching to chat mode — Hello there, Paimon, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ineffa? What are you doing here...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Varka placed a sizeable order with the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop. Aino is hard at work producing the strategic reserve, while I am handling the deliveries.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Secondly... I am also here to attend the meeting in her place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Flins! Paimon thought the Lightkeepers's rep would be Illuga or Nikita...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's not like you to volunteer to attend a meeting...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You're quite right — however, Illuga and Nikita are both busy organizing the Ratniki's region-wide response to the recent attacks.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: And since I'm well-acquainted with everyone else here... I was the one they recommended to attend the meeting.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Oh. So you don't even wanna be here!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Heh, sometimes you don't get a choice when there might be consequences down the line.

talks.objective: Command the team to feign a retreat

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hey, Honorary Knight. Looks like pretty much everyone's here.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Albedo and Durin are just wrapping up their analysis. You wanna wait for them here?

choices.text: (Wait for the meeting...)

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Great. While we're waiting, could you update me on the situation in Mondstadt?

choices.text: (Continue to mingle...)

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: That works too. Alright, you keep gathering intel.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ready... Fire!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The enemy has sustained heavy casualties. It should be a while before they're strong enough to pose a real threat again.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Use this time to catch your breath, and fill me in on everything you've learned.

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: We've narrowed down the search area for the final fragment to this zone here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...That's not exactly very "narrow"!

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: We split the search area between us and the Ratniki. Maybe they'll be able to narrow it down further?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Either way, I was about to go lend them a hand next anyway. Do you think you guys can keep up?

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: Absolutely! Good to go, Grand Master!

dialogues.speaker: Erminie
dialogues.text: We've run right through our supplies — we'll stay here and deal with any Wild Hunt that tries to stage a comeback.

dialogues.speaker: Erminie
dialogues.text: Now that they've lost their numerical advantage, they're no match for us. Focus on supporting the other team.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ready... Fire!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The enemy has sustained heavy casualties. It should be a while before they're strong enough to pose a real threat again.

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: Brave knights, on behalf of the Lightkeepers, I thank you for your assistance!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: There's no need to be so formal. When it comes to the Abyss, we're all in this together. Now, please tell me everything you've learned.

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: ...Very well.

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: We've narrowed down the search area for the final fragment to this zone here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...That's not exactly very "narrow"!

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: We split the search between us and the knights. Maybe they'll be able to narrow it down further?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Either way, I was about to go lend them a hand next anyway. Can I count on your help?

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: It would be our pleasure, Mr. Varka.

dialogues.speaker: Erminie
dialogues.text: We've run right through our supplies — we'll stay here and deal with any Wild Hunt that tries to stage a comeback.

dialogues.speaker: Erminie
dialogues.text: Now that they've lost their numerical advantage, they're no match for us. Focus on supporting the other team.

talks.objective: Command the Logistics Company to set up traps

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Fill me in. What's the situation?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: *sigh*... We ran into resistance almost as soon as we set off. Albedo said we should split into two teams and continue searching while he and the others kept the Wild Hunt occupied.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Good call. Locating the Wolf Spirit fragment is our key objective — I would have made the same decision.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Well, it seems the enemy figured as much too! Now both search teams are in big trouble... Oh, I brought a map — this should make things clearer.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Before we ran into trouble, this is the search area we'd decided on...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: The two teams are holed up here and here! They should have a clearer idea of the fragment's location by now.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...But the Wild Hunt is stopping them from relaying messages back, right? Do we have any more troops available to provide backup?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: We can't spare troops from any of the fronts right now. That just leaves us with—

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: The Logistics Company is standing by.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Ineffa!?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Designated drop point reached. Initiating situation report...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: The Logistics Company was assisting Aino with the production of the strategic reserve. But after learning of the situation on the front line, they requested to be dispatched immediately. They are currently nearby awaiting orders.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Amazing... Just in the nick of time.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Hey, seeing as you can fly and all... Shouldn't you be the one out here delivering messages!?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I regret to say that without the workshop's catapult, and with my short-distance propulsion module on cooldown, I will only be able to return to the battlefield after another five minutes. Please, keep up the good work, Jahoda.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: The Logistics Company has very limited provisions — only enough for a single battle... Which team should they support?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Both! Once one team has been rescued, the remaining forces will be free to support the other. We'll move out immediately — Jahoda, keep up the good work with the comms!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: *gulp*... S—Sure thing! Leave it to me, haha, hah... heh...

talks.objective: Command the team to feign a retreat
Go and assist the other squad

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ugh... Looks like the same situation here... They just keep coming, wave after wave.

dialogues.speaker: Virtanen
dialogues.text: Reinforcements? ...Hey! You keep them busy while we work on getting rid of this god-awful mist!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Understood! Everyone got that? It's up to us to hold them off!

dialogues.speaker: Knights
dialogues.text: ...Yes, sir!

talks.objective: Destroy the source of the Wild Hunt

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Phew... I'm glad that's finally over.

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: Brave knights, on behalf of the Lightkeepers, I thank you for your assistance!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: There's no need to be so formal. When it comes to the Abyss, we're all in this together. Now, please tell me everything you've learned.

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: ...Very well.

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: We've narrowed down the search area for the final fragment to this zone here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes! Now it feels like we're finally closing in on our target!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I'll say. We're sure to face fierce resistance from the Wild Hunt, though... Is everyone willing to keep fighting with us?

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: It would be our pleasure, Mr. Varka.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Much obliged. Alright, the target is just up ahead! Move out!

talks.objective: Go to the Wolf Spirit's location

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The hiding-in-the-mist trick again? Heh, these guys must be easily amused.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You all know the drill — the Knights of Favonius will engage the enemy while the Lightkeepers dispel the mist. Everyone, follow my signals!

dialogues.speaker: Everyone
dialogues.text: Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ugh! This Wild Hunt doesn't know when to give up!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Varka, you go on ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: Mr. Varka! Leave this to us!

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: Just like last time! Only a Knight of Boreas can deal with a Wolf Spirit, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ekbert
dialogues.text: Don't underestimate us, Grand Master! We can hold our own!

choices.text: And I'm here, too.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Huh... That's the spirit! Stay on your toes, and make the Knights of Favonius proud!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Either we all march back to Mondstadt together, or no one does!

choices.text: Now hurry up and go!

talks.objective: Go to the Wolf Spirit's location

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: It seems you have collected them all, Knight of Boreas.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Yeah, and with no corrupted fragments or ambushes along the way... I have to commend your chivalry, Sir Roland.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: A true knight does not resort to underhanded tactics. Were this body not a false one created by the Wild Hunt, nor would I countenance those monsters to taint our duel with their presence.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: If you need a moment to rest, take it. Victory will be mine, regardless of whether the path to it is the one I would wish for.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Save your breath! If you want to fight, let's fight!

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: As you wish... Then let us settle our unfinished duel here and now.

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: ...Is everyone alright?

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: Pff, my granny fights better than these rookies! It's Ekbert I'm worried about... You still alive?

dialogues.speaker: Ekbert
dialogues.text: Phew... For a moment there, I thought I might never taste the sweet wine of Mondstadt again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, stay put, you guys! Leave the rest to us!

dialogues.speaker: Ekbert
dialogues.text: Forget us... We can take care of ourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: You're the only ones still standing... Honorary Knight, find the Grand Master!

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: We can't lose our Varka... Please, you have to find him!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Got it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Varka... I hope your plan is still gonna work...)

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hmph!

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: You're holding back, Knight of Boreas. I can tell you do not wish to strike me down.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: This duel does no justice to the way of chivalry. I wield the power of a god, while you dare not swing your sword with true intent. If you continue on this path, you will die.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Your plan is doomed to fail. How can a helpless lamb hope to tame the heart of a wolf when the wolf has seen through the lamb's plan?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha... You're onto me already, huh?

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Andrius's question, Boreas's answer, the means to bear a soul... I knew it all five hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Though the false path may be wide and welcoming, only destruction lies at its end. It is time to crush your futile hope...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: It's over. Your sword lies shattered. The Wolf Spirit and the thoughts you blindly placed your faith in have nowhere left to dwell

dialogues.speaker: "Roland"
dialogues.text: Join me, and pledge your allegiance to the Abyss, Knight of Boreas. One day, you will understand that the only righteous path for those of true virtue is the path of darkest truths.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Varka!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: (For the next part, it's over to you...)

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: (...Outlander Who Caught the Wind!)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Jahoda, you dummy... You took this stupid job of your own free will! Crying isn't gonna get you out of it!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Remnant fragments of an ancient god... thoughts stored inside a blade... Maybe I'm overthinking this, but I suspect there is more to Mr. Varka's plan than what he's revealed to us so far.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmm... Then again, the enemy can harness the Wild Hunt to spy on us wherever we go. As our commander, I'm sure he has his reasons for choosing not to tell us everything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The meeting's probably gonna be in the biggest tent, right? Looks like a bunch of people are there already. Why don't we go chat with them?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, when this is all over, I'm gonna invite you around for a drink of—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa! Stop thinking about Mondstadt's wine and keep your head in the game! You can't be daydreaming about alcohol before a battle!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Huh? Alright, just trying to lift our spirits a little... Uh... Oh — you wanna see some photos I took of me and the knights before the expedition, maybe?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shut up, shut up, shut up! Can we please just focus on finding the Wolf Spirit fragment!?

dialogues.speaker: Erminie
dialogues.text: Logistics Company! Deploy!

dialogues.speaker: Ekbert
dialogues.text: Grand Master! Honorary Knight! Thank goodness you're here!

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Be careful! There's no end to these monsters... however many we kill, more keep coming!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Just as I thought... Well, they're about to get a shock to the system — we'll wipe 'em out faster than they can replenish their numbers! We just have to hold on until the Logistics Company is ready!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Is that the signal to say they're ready?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: It's showtime! Fall back!

dialogues.speaker: Knights
dialogues.text: ...Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hey! They're running out of steam — now's your chance!

dialogues.speaker: Virtanen
dialogues.text: Affirmative! Sorry to keep you waiting!

dialogues.speaker: Vytautas
dialogues.text: That's their source — it was hidden in the mist! If we destroy that, the Wild Hunt won't be able to summon any more reinforcements!

dialogues.speaker: Winfried
dialogues.text: Knights of Favonius, charge!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Argh...!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: (...The final fragment is right there... Don't let me down.)
